svg.title: Protest, Rotten Boroughs & The Road to Democracy (1819–1872)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 8 historical GIS atlas map of Great Britain and unpartitioned Ireland (1819–1872) contrasting unrepresented northern industrial cities (0 MPs pre-1832) and the 1819 Peterloo Massacre in Manchester with southern rotten boroughs like Old Sarum and Dunwich, the 1830 Hampshire Captain Swing riots and 1834 Tolpuddle Martyrs, the October 1831 Bristol Reform Riots, London’s Chartist rallies at Kennington Common, and the 1872 Secret Ballot Act at Pontefract.

g.text: 1872 Secret Ballot Act → First Vote at Pontefract

text.tspan: Deserted mound (7 voters, 2 MPs) & eroded coast
Three-day uprising after Lords block reform
helps force the 1832 Great Reform Act
Chartist People’s Charter rallies pave the way

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 8 ENQUIRY: INDUSTRIALISATION & REFORM (1750–1872)
Protest, Rotten Boroughs & The Road to Democracy (1819–1872)
Before 1832, deserted “rotten boroughs” like Old Sarum elected 2 MPs while industrial Manchester, Birmingham, and Leeds had zero.
From Peterloo (1819) and Bristol (1831) to the Chartists, popular pressure won the 1832 Reform Act and 1872 Secret Ballot Act.
